ukmt-sk-2018-03.title: Sine rule
ukmt-sk-2018-03.body:
$\frac{\sin\angle ABC}{AC}=\frac{\sin30^\circ}{BC}$ gives $\sin\angle ABC=\frac{5\sqrt2\cdot\frac12}{5}=\frac{\sqrt2}2$, so $\angle ABC=45^\circ$ or $135^\circ$ (both give a valid triangle since $45+30<180$ and $135+30<180$). The largest is $135^\circ$.

**Answer: 135**

ukmt-sk-2018-04.title: Divide the products
ukmt-sk-2018-04.body:
Let the list be $60,x,y,z,300$. Then $60xy=810000$ gives $xy=13500$; $xyz=2430000$ gives $z=180$; $300yz=8100000$ gives $yz=27000$, so $y=\frac{27000}{180}=150$ (and $x=90$). The third number is $150$.

**Answer: 150**

ukmt-sk-2018-05.title: Sequences with no two equal wins in a row
ukmt-sk-2018-05.body:
Neither is champion after three games exactly when the results of the first three games (R = Rachel wins, S = Steven wins, D = draw) contain no $RR$ and no $SS$. Condition on the first two results and then on what the third may be:

- $RS$: $0.6\cdot0.3=0.18$, third game not won by Steven ($0.7$): $0.126$
- $RD$: $0.06$, third game anything: $0.06$
- $SR$: $0.18$, third not won by Rachel ($0.4$): $0.072$
- $SD$: $0.03$
- $DR$: $0.06$, third not won by Rachel ($0.4$): $0.024$
- $DS$: $0.03$, third not won by Steven ($0.7$): $0.021$
- $DD$: $0.01$

Sum: $0.126+0.06+0.072+0.03+0.024+0.021+0.01=0.343$, so $1000P=343$.

**Answer: 343**

ukmt-sk-2018-06.title: Power of the point $S$
ukmt-sk-2018-06.body:
Let $YS=a$. In circle $C_2$ (through $Q,R,X,Y$): $SR\cdot SQ=SY\cdot SX$, so $9\cdot16=a(a+18)$, giving $a=6$. Then $SX=24$ and $WX=6a=36$, so $SW=60$.

In circle $C_1$ (through $P,Q,W,X$): $SQ\cdot SP=SX\cdot SW$, so $16\cdot SP=24\cdot60$ and $SP=90$. Therefore $PS+WS=90+60=150$.

**Answer: 150**

ukmt-sk-2018-07.title: Solve for the edge
ukmt-sk-2018-07.body:
For edge $x$: volume plus surface area is $x^3+6x^2$ and the sum of the edges is $12x$, so $x^3+6x^2=\frac43\cdot12x=16x$. Dividing by $x>0$: $x^2+6x-16=0$, $(x-2)(x+8)=0$, so $x=2$. Twenty-seven cubes have volume $27\cdot8=216$.

**Answer: 216**

ukmt-sk-2018-08.title: Find the range of $x$
ukmt-sk-2018-08.body:
$x^2\le729$ means $-27\le x\le27$. $729\le-x^3$ means $x^3\le-729=(-9)^3$, i.e. $x\le-9$. So $-27\le x\le-9$ and the largest difference is $P-Q=-9-(-27)=18$. The answer is $10\times18=180$.

**Answer: 180**

ukmt-sk-2018-09.title: Totals
ukmt-sk-2018-09.body:
Class 7A has $15$ boys and $15$ girls; 7B has $25$ boys and $5$ girls; there are $20$ girls and $40$ boys. All girls score $20\cdot60=1200$ in total; 7A's girls score $15\cdot48=720$, so 7B's girls score $480$, a mean of $96$. Hence the $15$ boys of 7A have mean $48$ and total $720$. Everyone scores $60\cdot60=3600$, so the boys score $2400$ in total, and 7B's $25$ boys score $2400-720=1680$: $\mu=\frac{1680}{25}=67.2$ and $10\mu=672$.

**Answer: 672**

ukmt-sk-2018-11.title: Generate the sequence
ukmt-sk-2018-11.body:
The sequence is $2,1,3,4,5,6,7,8,11,9,13,10,17,12,19,14,23,15,29,\dots$ Before $U_{19}=29$ every step differs by at most $10$ (the largest earlier jump is $23-14=9$), and $U_{19}-U_{18}=29-15=14>10$. So $k=18$, $U_k=15$ and $k\times U_k=270$.

**Answer: 270**

ukmt-sk-2018-12.title: Diagonals
ukmt-sk-2018-12.body:
The two tilted squares span the width of the wall, so their diagonals add up to $16$: each diagonal is $8$ m and each has area $\frac{8^2}2=32$. The large square's side equals a tilted square's diagonal, $8$, so its area is $64$. Total $B=32+32+64=128$.

**Answer: 128**

ukmt-sk-2018-13.title: Digits and divisibility
ukmt-sk-2018-13.body:
No digit is $0$, nine digits sum to $10$, so eight of them are $1$ and one is $2$. The number is odd, so the $2$ is not last: eight candidates. Testing divisibility by $7$, only $112\,111\,111$ works ($=7\times16\,015\,873$). To three significant figures it is $112$ million.

**Answer: 112**

ukmt-sk-2018-14.title: Coordinates
ukmt-sk-2018-14.body:
Put $A=(0,0)$, $B=(40,0)$, $C=(40,40)$, $D=(0,40)$, so $F=(0,20)$. Since $CG:GF=2:3$, $G=C+\frac25(F-C)=(40-16,\,40-8)=(24,32)$. Triangle $BCG$ has base $BC=40$ and height equal to the horizontal distance from $G$ to line $BC$, $40-24=16$. Area $=\frac12\cdot40\cdot16=320$.

**Answer: 320**

ukmt-sk-2018-15.title: Find the period
ukmt-sk-2018-15.body:
The terms are $20,18,2,20,-18,2,-20,-18,-2,-20,18,-2,20,18,\dots$: the sequence repeats with period $12$ and each period sums to $0$. Since $2018=12\cdot168+2$, the sum is that of the first two terms of a period: $20+18=38$.

**Answer: 38**

ukmt-sk-2018-16.title: Two cases
ukmt-sk-2018-16.body:
If $20$ is the hypotenuse, $20^2-a^2$ must be a square: $a=12$ (with $16$) works, so $20$ is in the list. If $20$ is a leg with other leg $b$ and hypotenuse $h$: $(h-b)(h+b)=400$ with both factors of the same parity: $(2,200),(4,100),(8,50),(10,40)$ give $h=101,52,29,25$ (the pairs $(1,400),(5,80),(16,25)$ have mixed parity and $(20,20)$ gives $b=0$). The hypotenuses are $20,25,29,52,101$, with sum $227$.

**Answer: 227**

ukmt-sk-2018-18.title: Count factors of 5
ukmt-sk-2018-18.body:
The exponent of $2$ exceeds the exponent of $5$ everywhere here, so the number of trailing zeros equals the exponent of $5$. By Legendre, $v_5(2018!)=403+80+16+3=502$, $v_5(30!)=6+1=7$ and $v_5(11!)=2$. So the quotient has $502-7-2=493$ trailing zeros.

**Answer: 493**

ukmt-sk-2018-19.title: Two cases
ukmt-sk-2018-19.body:
$(2x-y)^4=1$ with real numbers means $2x-y=\pm1$. Multiply by $y$ and use $xy=15$: if $2x-y=1$ then $30-y^2=y$, so $y=5$ or $-6$; if $2x-y=-1$ then $30-y^2=-y$, so $y=6$ or $-5$. (All four have a real $x=15/y$.) So $z=25+36+25+36=122$.

**Answer: 122**
